## Summary

This page lists environment variables that the checked-in sources read or inject. It includes deployment helpers, Kubernetes templates, skills, tools, and image entrypoints. It also includes inputs to development tools. A source reference proves that a file uses the name. It does not prove that every deployment sets the variable.

The Surface column identifies the receiving process. A `maintainer-verification-input` controls a development tool, such as its input directory. Set it only when you run that tool. It does not configure a running product service. The consumer-specific contract identifies the tool, its accepted values, and its errors.

## Choose the receiving process before setting a value

1. Find the variable, then select the consumer source for the command or workload you are configuring. The same name can have different defaults and validation in different processes.
2. Read that consumer's accepted form, empty-value behavior, precedence, and failure boundary. Precedence is local to that consumer; table order does not define a global override order.
3. Follow the Surface guidance. For an injected value, change the owning Helm, GitOps, Secret, or generated-configuration input. Do not export a competing terminal value. An internal shell assignment is not an operator setting.
4. Verify the effective workload configuration and the consumer's documented health or failure signal. Source references, table generation, and syntax checks do not prove that a deployed process received the value.

Embedded Node or Python readers inside shell scripts and YAML payloads are receiving processes too. Their presence does not make their inputs externally configurable. An injection-only row proves a producer, not the receiving program's defaults or validation; use the named external authority before changing it. Secret classifications describe provenance and handling, not verified live access control. Do not print Secret values when checking effective configuration.

## Configuration-Selected Variable Names

Some runtime configuration fields select an environment variable name. These names are not a fixed list. Set the named variable in the actual receiving process and follow the configuration field's conditions. The example names on the linked configuration page are examples, not the only supported names.

| Configuration field and source | Purpose and condition | Accepted form | Default, empty, invalid, and precedence | Impact and failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tokenEnvironmentVariable` in [`loadProductionBusterRemotePlanRuntime`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L143-L143)<br>[Runtime configuration](buster-runtime-configuration.md)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:127`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L127-L127)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:138`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L138-L141)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:144`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L144-L144)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:143`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L143-L143) | Selects the environment variable that contains the remote-test bearer token when the selected authentication mode requires it.<br>Required: required only without trustedPeerSpiffeIds<br>Condition: Only when trustedPeerSpiffeIds is absent. | A variable name matching `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`; its non-empty contents supply the bearer token. | Default: No selector default. The configuration file selects an arbitrary supported variable name; documented examples are not a closed allow-list.<br>Empty: In the selected SPIFFE mode the token selector is not read. In bearer mode, a missing, empty, or malformed selector is rejected; an absent or empty selected variable returns BUSTER_REMOTE_CONFIG_TOKEN_MISSING.<br>Invalid: An invalid selector returns BUSTER_REMOTE_CONFIG_TOKEN_ENV_INVALID; downstream bearer verification rejects unusable credentials.<br>Precedence: The canonical JSON file selects the key; the function environment argument supplies its contents and defaults to the current process environment. The selected SPIFFE mode bypasses only bearer-token selection. | Impact: Changing the selector changes the bearer credential used for the non-SPIFFE remote-plan transport.<br>Failure: Configuration loading stops before remote-plan work is admitted when its selected required variable is missing or unusable. |
| `sourceAttestationPublicKeyEnvironmentVariable` in [`loadProductionBusterRemotePlanRuntime`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L150-L150)<br>[Runtime configuration](buster-runtime-configuration.md)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:127`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L127-L127)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:147`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L147-L149)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:151`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L151-L151)<br>[`skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts:150`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/5be36e11c830c8312e0ca0c13deed17a6ccab1a4/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/production.ts#L150-L150) | Selects the environment variable that contains the Nova source-attestation trusted public key.<br>Required: required<br>Condition: Always required by the selected remote-test runtime. | A variable name matching `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`, different from the selected token variable; its non-empty contents supply the required source-attestation key. | Default: No selector default. The configuration file selects an arbitrary supported variable name; documented examples are not a closed allow-list.<br>Empty: A missing, empty, or malformed selector is rejected; an absent or empty selected variable returns BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PUBLIC_KEY_MISSING.<br>Invalid: An invalid or reused selector returns BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_ENV_INVALID; downstream Ed25519 verification rejects unusable public-key bytes.<br>Precedence: The canonical JSON file selects the key; the function environment argument supplies its contents and defaults to the current process environment. ## Ownership And Runtime Boundaries

| Variable group | Owner | Runtime effect | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Namespace and workspace prompt | `scripts/deploy.sh`; `my-values/setup-secrets.sh` | selects the Kubernetes namespace and optionally records `my-values/.workspace-namespace` for local operator convenience | `./scripts/deploy.sh status`; generated inventory check |
| Component switches | `scripts/deploy.sh`; `my-values/setup-secrets.sh` | controls optional PostgreSQL, LiteLLM, and Tailscale setup paths; `ALLOW_PARTIAL_INFRA` changes rollout failures from fail-closed to warning | deployment truth plus live rollout status |
| Secret setup controls | `my-values/setup-secrets.sh` | chooses interactive/noninteractive/auto resolution, overwrite behavior, source namespace copies, and Tailscale OAuth bootstrap | `kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get secret ...`; `kubectl -n "$TAILSCALE_OPERATOR_NAMESPACE" get secret operator-oauth` |
| Code bundle selection | `scripts/deploy.sh` | derives GitHub release bundle URLs from repository + commit unless explicit archive URLs are provided | `NOVA_CODE_BUNDLE_EXPECTED_COMMIT=<sha> ./scripts/deploy.sh code nova`; `BUSTER_CODE_BUNDLE_EXPECTED_COMMIT=<sha> ./scripts/deploy.sh code buster` |

## Failure Modes

- Invalid boolean-like values can skip expected component paths or keep optional setup enabled; use the exact values listed in this table.
- Noninteractive secret setup warns when a required source is unavailable instead of inventing credentials.
- `ALLOW_PARTIAL_INFRA=true` is for troubleshooting only; the default infra path should fail closed on required rollout failures.
- Code deploy requires the expected commit for each targeted agent. Private repositories also require a bundle auth Secret for GitHub release assets.
